description: Defining, provisioning and maintaining infrastructure as version-controlled code: the case for automation, declarative provisioning with Terraform, reusable modules, state and drift, configuration management with Ansible, testing infrastructure, policy as code and GitOps workflows. Practised in simulated terminals and a simulated cloud console in the browser, where every plan and apply shows its effect on real-looking resources, taught to the depth of the infrastructure automation certifications.
modelledOn: Morris, Infrastructure as Code: Dynamic Systems for the Cloud Age
outcomes: Justify infrastructure as code by contrasting it with manual, ticket-driven provisioning and identify where it fails.
Write declarative Terraform configurations that provision networks, compute, storage and identity on a cloud platform.
Design reusable, versioned modules and structure code for multiple environments and teams.
Manage remote state safely, detect and reconcile drift, and import existing resources.
Configure servers idempotently with Ansible and choose between immutable and mutable infrastructure.
Test infrastructure code, enforce policy and deliver changes through GitOps workflows with review and audit.

units.title: Why infrastructure as code
topics: The problems of manual provisioning: snowflake servers, configuration drift, undocumented changes, slow recovery
Principles: everything in version control, idempotence, repeatability, disposability, small changes
Declarative versus imperative tools; provisioning versus configuration management; the tool landscape
Infrastructure as code in a team: code review for infrastructure, change records, blast radius

units.title: Declarative provisioning
topics: HCL syntax: providers, resources, data sources, variables, outputs, locals
The workflow: init, plan, apply, destroy; reading a plan; the dependency graph and parallelism
Expressions: count, for_each, conditionals, dynamic blocks, built-in functions
Provisioning a VPC, subnets, security groups, virtual machines and object storage
Cloud-native alternatives in brief: CloudFormation, Bicep, Pulumi and OpenTofu

units.title: Modules and reuse
topics: Writing modules: inputs, outputs, encapsulation; root and child modules
Module sources and versioning: registries, Git tags, semantic versioning
Composing modules into stacks; environment layouts for development, staging and production
Workspaces versus separate directories; managing differences with variable files
A reusable module for a three-tier web application used by several teams

units.title: State and drift
topics: What state is and why it exists: mapping configuration to real resources
Remote backends, state locking and encryption; secrets that leak into state
Drift: how it happens, detecting it with refresh and plan, deciding whether to revert or adopt
Refactoring safely: moved blocks, state mv, rm and import; splitting large states
Recovering from a corrupted or lost state file

units.title: Configuration management
topics: Ansible architecture: inventories, ad hoc commands, playbooks, modules, agentless SSH
Idempotent tasks, handlers, variables, facts and templates with Jinja2
Roles and collections; Ansible Vault for secrets
Immutable infrastructure: building golden images with Packer versus configuring running servers
Configuring a fleet of servers for a mobile money agent network, with Terraform and Ansible working together

units.title: Testing infrastructure
topics: The testing pyramid for infrastructure: formatting, validation, static analysis, unit, integration, end-to-end
Linting and security scanning: tflint, Checkov, tfsec; ansible-lint
Native terraform test, Terratest and Molecule; ephemeral test environments and their cost
Policy as code with Open Policy Agent and Sentinel: blocking public buckets and enforcing data residency rules
Cost estimation in pull requests

units.title: GitOps workflows
topics: GitOps principles: Git as the source of truth, declarative desired state, pull-based reconciliation
CI/CD for infrastructure: plan on pull request, apply on merge, approvals and protected environments
Argo CD and Flux for Kubernetes; Atlantis and similar tools for Terraform
Secrets in GitOps: sealed secrets, external secret operators, short-lived credentials with OIDC

units.title: Operating infrastructure as code at scale
topics: Disaster recovery by rebuilding from code; tested recovery times
Platform engineering and self-service infrastructure; golden paths
Compliance and audit: change history, tagging standards, data residency under the Data Protection Act
Capstone: provision, configure, test and deliver through GitOps a complete environment, then detect and fix injected drift
